canonical.title: Print the Longest Common Subsequence
canonical.sourceFilePath: 14. Dynamic Programming/5. DP on Strings/02. Print the LCS.cpp

narrative.title: The Firmware Lineage Tracer
narrative.scenario: A hardware team tracks two firmware branches and must print the exact sequence of module tokens both branches inherited from their common ancestor — not just how many. The lineage tool rebuilds the shared token string by walking the completion table backwards, emitting each token where the branches agree.
narrative.inputFormat: Integers n and m, plus strings s1 and s2 of lengths n and m.
narrative.outputFormat: Return one longest common subsequence as a string. If several exist, any valid one is accepted.
constraints: strings consist of uppercase or lowercase English letters

testCases.explanation: "ace" appears in order within both strings and no longer anchor exists.
"ac" also has length 2, so "bc" is an equally valid reconstruction.

hintLevels: Level 1: Build the usual length table first — reconstruction always starts from a finished table.
Level 2: From (n, m), step diagonally on a match (emit the character), otherwise move toward the larger neighbor.
Level 3: Characters come out backwards; reverse once at the end.
